correctness.rationale: PASS. With B=beta uu*, define a=beta^(1-t) A^t u and b=beta^t A^(1-t)u. Then C=a u*+u b* has at most two singular values and H=(a+b)u* has rank one. Hilbert–Schmidt expansion yields 2 beta K for ||H||_2^2-||C||_2^2; exterior-square Gram determinants give s1*s2=beta sqrt(V_F V_G), hence trace defect 2 beta(sqrt(V_F V_G)-K). Increasing power functions yield K>0 exactly for nonsingleton spectral support. Cauchy–Schwarz equality means two powers are affinely related on spectral support, and strict convexity/concavity forces at most two support points unless t=1/2. With strictly positive second singular value, Schatten-p norm of C is strictly decreasing whereas H norm is constant, yielding one crossover in (1,2) for >=3 supports and t≠1/2. Independent 3x3 matrix SVD agrees with 1004/3, 952/3 and exact trace defect. Boundary t=1/2 and 1/2-point supports checked analytically. Finite SVD only corroborates the universal proof.
residual_risks: Only B positive rank one, t strictly between 0 and 1; no universal arbitrary-rank B ordering.
The 3D witness does not prove infinite-dimensional quantifiers.
